paragraphs: (Talmai king of Geshur, [II Samuel 3:3](https://www.sefaria.org/II_Samuel.3.3).) In [Megillah 9a](https://www.sefaria.org/Megillah.9a.11-16) and [Tractate Soferim 1:8](https://www.sefaria.org/Tractate_Soferim.1.8) it is related that he gathered seventy-two elders and told them to write for him the Torah of Moses (to translate it into Greek), and all of them agreed on one view and changed thirteen things in it, writing “God created in the beginning,” “I shall make man,” “And He finished on the sixth day and rested on the seventh,” etc. At the end of Megillat Taanit: on the eighth of Tevet the Torah was written in Greek in the days of King Ptolemy, and darkness came upon the world for three days.[^1]

Hyman reports from the Jewish Antiquities, chapter 2 that after the death of Alexander of Macedon, Ptolemy Soter reigned forty years, and after him Ptolemy Philadelphus reigned thirty-nine years. He had a keeper of his library, a man of noble spirit named Demetrius of Phalerum, who advised the king to have the books of the Torah translated for him; his faithful friend Aristeas also helped in this. The High Priest then was Elazar, brother of Shimon HaTzaddik. The king wrote to him to send him the choicest of the sages of Israel to translate the Torah scroll, and in the course of seventy-two days they completed their great work. The king rejoiced greatly at this, sent precious gifts to the Temple and to the High Priest, and did good to all Israel.

In [Soferim 1:7](https://www.sefaria.org/Tractate_Soferim.1.7): an incident with five elders who wrote the Torah in Greek for King Ptolemy, and the day was as hard for Israel as the day on which the calf was made, for the Torah could not be translated fully as needed.[^2]

notes.text: The biblical parenthesis refers to Talmai of Geshur. Megillah and Soferim tell the seventy-two-elder account. Soferim gives the figure of thirteen changes. The Megillah list continues on [the next folio](https://www.sefaria.org/Megillah.9b.1-3).

The five-elder account is a separate episode in Soferim. [Shulchan Arukh](https://www.sefaria.org/Shulchan_Arukh%2C_Orach_Chayim.580.2) also gives the eighth of Tevet and three days of darkness. The reign lengths and the seventy-two days in Hyman’s account of Josephus are his historical report.
